scan.summary: This is an Emergency Action Plan for Cascade Specialty Chemicals' Portland facility covering fire, chemical release, medical emergency, earthquake and other emergencies. It describes alarm systems, evacuation procedures, employee accountability, rescue and medical response, and training requirements for all 42 employees plus contractors and visitors. The plan names specific assembly points, roles (floor wardens, first-aid responders), and response protocols for normal evacuation and shelter-in-place scenarios.
scan.freshness_note: This document was revised in February 2021, nearly 5.5 years old as of September 2026. Given that the plan states it is reviewed every January by the facilities lead and updated when building layout changes, an updated version should be on file. Request a current copy to confirm this is still the active plan and that all employee rosters and evacuation maps reflect present conditions.

gaps.title: Emergency contact information
gaps.description: The plan does not specify emergency contact procedures, phone numbers for emergency services, or how to contact the incident coordinator. It does not state who the incident coordinator is or how they are identified during an emergency.
gaps.fix: Add a section listing emergency phone numbers (911, poison control, local fire department non-emergency line), the name and contact method for the incident coordinator, and secondary contacts if the primary is unavailable.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.38(e) requires the plan to include procedures for employees to report fires and other emergencies
gaps.locator: Section 1 or new section on emergency contacts; not in document

gaps.title: Procedure for chemical release inside the building
gaps.description: The plan describes shelter-in-place for outdoor chemical hazards but does not specify what to do for a chemical release or spill inside the building. It does not address containment, notification procedures, or use of spill kits.
gaps.fix: Add a section addressing indoor chemical spills and releases: identify response procedures (e.g., isolate area, notify supervisor), the location and use of spill kits, when to call emergency services vs. when to contain, and procedures for notifying regulatory agencies if required.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.38 requires specific procedures for different types of emergencies; OSHA expects plans to address fire, chemical release, medical emergency, and natural disaster separately.
gaps.locator: Section 3 (Evacuation procedures) only addresses outdoor chemical release; not in document for indoor scenario
gaps.quote: For a chemical release outdoors or a hazard that makes leaving the building unsafe, the shelter-in-place signal sounds.

gaps.title: Regulatory agency notification
gaps.description: The plan does not address notification of regulatory agencies (Oregon DEQ, local fire marshal, EPA) in case of a chemical release or environmental contamination. It names only fire department notification.
gaps.fix: Add procedures stating who is responsible for notifying Oregon DEQ and any other required agencies for chemical releases that meet reportable thresholds, including required information to provide and timelines for notification.
gaps.citation: OAR 340-122-050 and related Oregon environmental regulations require notification of environmental releases; 29 CFR 1910.38(e) requires the plan to include proper reporting
gaps.locator: Section 1 or new section; not in document

gaps.title: Review and update frequency not documented
gaps.description: The plan states the facilities lead reviews the plan every January, but there is no documentation, log, or process for recording when reviews occur, what changes were made, or who performed the review. OSHA expects to see evidence that reviews happened.
gaps.fix: Create and maintain a log showing the date of each annual review, the name of the person who reviewed it, what changes were made (if any), and the signature or initials of the reviewer. Include this log as an appendix or keep it separate with the plan.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.38(g) requires the employer to review the plan with all employees and update it when necessary; recordkeeping of reviews is expected practice
gaps.locator: Section 6 (Training and review); not in document
gaps.quote: The facilities lead reviews the plan every January and updates the evacuation maps whenever the building layout changes.

gaps.title: Missing appendices in document
gaps.description: The plan references Appendix A (Evacuation maps) and Appendix B (Floor warden and first-aid responder roster) but these are not included in the PDF provided. Without these, it cannot be verified that the plan is complete or that roles and escape routes are actually documented.
gaps.fix: Obtain and review Appendix A and Appendix B. Verify that evacuation maps show all exits, assembly point, and escape routes for warehouse, laboratory, and offices. Verify that the roster lists all current floor wardens (one per area) and first-aid responders (two per shift) with their names.
gaps.citation: 29 CFR 1910.38(c) requires written procedures for exits and escape routes to be clearly marked; 29 CFR 1910.37 requires exit maps
gaps.quote:
Appendix A: Evacuation maps (warehouse, laboratory, offices)
Appendix B: Floor warden and first-aid responder roster (posted beside each evacuation map)

gaps.title: Procedures for disabled or mobility-limited employees
gaps.description: The plan does not address how employees with disabilities, mobility limitations, or injuries that prevent them from using standard exits and assembly points would be evacuated or protected. This is especially critical for a facility with 42 employees and contractors.
gaps.fix: Add a section addressing evacuations for employees with disabilities or temporary mobility limitations. Identify designated safe areas where they can wait for assistance, designate employees trained to assist them, and establish procedures for contacting emergency responders about persons needing assistance.
gaps.citation: ADA Title II and Title III require reasonable accommodations for emergency procedures; OSHA guidance on emergency action plans includes addressing employees with disabilities (OSHA 3088)

gaps.title: No mention of communication systems for deaf or hard-of-hearing employees
gaps.description: The alarm system is described as 'audible horns and strobe lights' but the plan does not explicitly state that the strobe lights serve employees who are deaf or hard of hearing, or whether visual alarms are in all work areas where such employees may be stationed.
gaps.fix: Confirm that strobe lights are installed in all work areas (warehouse, laboratory, loading dock, offices) where deaf or hard-of-hearing employees work, or add a statement in the plan explaining how these employees will be alerted to an emergency.
gaps.citation: ADA requires effective emergency notification systems accessible to people with hearing disabilities; 29 CFR 1910.38(c) requires alarms to be perceivable by all employees
gaps.quote: The building has a monitored fire alarm system with audible horns and strobe lights in the warehouse, laboratory, loading dock and offices.

expected_missing.title: Chemical Hygiene Plan or Safety Data Sheet (SDS) inventory
expected_missing.why: Chemical distribution companies must maintain SDS for all chemicals in inventory and have them accessible during emergencies (OSHA Hazard Communication Standard 29 CFR 1910.1200)

expected_missing.title: Hazard communication training records
expected_missing.why: Employees handling chemicals must be trained on hazard communication, labeling, and SDS use (29 CFR 1910.1200(h))

expected_missing.title: Fire prevention plan
expected_missing.why: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.38(a) requires employers to develop a fire prevention plan; the Emergency Action Plan is separate from but related to the fire prevention plan

expected_missing.title: Records of evacuation drills and attendance
expected_missing.why: OSHA expects to see documented records of the twice-yearly drills showing who participated and any issues identified

expected_missing.title: Medical emergency procedures and first-aid training certification
expected_missing.why: Documentation that the two first-aid responders per shift hold valid first-aid and CPR certifications

expected_missing.title: Spill response procedures and spill kit inventory
expected_missing.why: Chemical distributors must have procedures for responding to chemical spills and maintain spill response equipment

expected_missing.title: Incident coordinator appointment and contact information
expected_missing.why: The plan references an 'incident coordinator' but does not name who holds this role or how they are designated

scan.confidence_notes: High confidence in what the document says: I read the full text directly. High confidence that this is an Emergency Action Plan required under 29 CFR 1910.38. Moderate confidence on gaps: I am confident about the missing regulatory notification procedures, accessibility for disabled employees, and documentation practices based on OSHA standards. I am less certain about the specific Oregon DEQ notification thresholds without checking current regulations. The document is 5.5 years old, and I am highly confident this version is out of date and should be updated. I did not receive Appendices A and B, so I cannot verify that evacuation maps and rosters are complete. I am confident in identifying missing sections based on OSHA 1910.38 and related standards, though I have not verified current emergency notification rule changes since February 2021.
